correctness.rationale: Reconstructed exact updates of the m-1 ordinary clique vertices (unanimous after one step for odd m; unanimous/bit-complement critical split for even m) and hub threshold. A frozen adjacent equal-bit pair on the path propagates an absorbing front; otherwise alternating path bits move the front no earlier than the computed sharp time. The critical even case uses a first equal-pair index and the explicit three-step return to unanimity. Counted odd balanced-clique extremizers and two disjoint even classes, including endpoint ell=2 and clique m=3. Independently rebuilt adjacency/update map and exhaustive state trajectories for m=3..7 and ell=2..5; all exact extrema, extremizer descriptions, and 2-cycle classification passed. This finite check corroborates but does not establish the all-size front proof.

value.rationale: A clique-path lollipop is a natural extremal testbed for deterministic majority convergence. Sharp parity-dependent delay with exact counts and a full recurrent-state classification isolates how a high-degree clique interacts with a one-dimensional propagation bottleneck; this is not merely the known global bound or a small experimental value.

final_claim: For binary synchronous strict open-neighbor majority with tie retention on a labelled clique K_m joined at one hub to an ell-vertex path, m>=3, ell>=2, the maximum first period-at-most-two entry is ell+2 for odd m and ell+1 for even m, with respective extremizer counts 2*binom(m-1,(m-1)/2) and 2^(m-1); only even m have primitive two-periodic states, all initially periodic.
limitations: m>=3, ell>=2; labelled finite simple clique plus a single terminal path; binary synchronous strict neighbor majority with tie retention only.
